enrichment.markdown:
- **Bialystoker Tageblatt.** The Białystok Yizkor history supplies a fuller newspaper record: it dates the paper’s appearance to **1913**, names **A. S. Herszberg** as editor, and identifies **David Sohn** as its American correspondent. The same account lists other Jewish papers, distinguishing the *Tageblatt* from *Unzer Leben*, which it says sustained daily publication for twenty years. This is useful context for the paper’s place in Białystok’s press, but the source does not give the *Tageblatt*’s run dates or explain when or why it ceased. [Białystok Yizkor history, “The Jewish Press in Bialystok”](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia036.html)

- **Rabbi Szabsaj Walach, Mojsze Walach and Awrom Jakow.** The Yizkor account connects these relatives to Meir Walach, later known as **Maxim Litvinov**: Szabsaj was his grandfather and a spiritual leader in Rozenoj; Mojsze was his father, a Talmud scholar who worked as a bank controller in Białystok; Awrom Jakow was his uncle and a textile manufacturer in Łódź. A separate passage identifies **Rabbi Jakow Walach** as Litvinov’s older brother and recounts a 1938 interview with him in Białystok. These are family details from the community history, not independent archival corroboration; the passages do not supply birth, death, emigration or Holocaust-fate records for the named relatives. [Family account](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia036.html) · [Interview with Rabbi Jakow Walach](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia036.html)

- **Rozenoj and Slonim.** The account places Szabsaj’s rabbinic role in Rozenoj, described as near Slonim. The material located here does not add a precise address or further biographical record for him in either place. [Białystok Yizkor history](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia036.html)

- **Bialystok Kehilla and the New York relief committee.** The Kehilla was more than a religious authority: the history describes communal health, welfare, burial, refugee relief and educational functions. It also records that Białystok received relief funds from the Bialystoker organization in New York in 1919, and that a committee delegate arrived in 1920. A separate account says the New York committee was founded in 1919 and describes aid sent to Białystok and surrounding towns. [Kehilla and chronology](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia036.html) · [Relief Committee history](https://jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/bia162.html)

- **Ivy Love, Walter Love, H. G. Wells and London.** I found no relevant match in the searched JewishGen/Yizkor material for these names in connection with the newspaper or the Walach family. The available material also did not establish how these people connect to the paper; same-name matches elsewhere would not be enough to identify them.

- **Search limits.** I searched JewishGen/Yizkor for the newspaper and the family and place names, including **Walach/Walach**, **Szabsaj**, **Mojsze**, and **Awrom Jakow**, and checked the listed names in combinations. I did not find usable results in the permitted search results from YIVO, Yad Vashem, USHMM, Arolsen, or Geni for the Love names or the other connected people. Absence from these searches is not proof that no records exist.
